description: The tribal population in India is a significant part of the country's cultural and demographic diversity. According to the 2011 Census, Scheduled Tribes account for 8.6% of India's total population.

sections.title: Constitutional Provisions and Concepts
sections.description: The Constitution of India contains several provisions for the identification and protection of the rights of tribal communities.

key_concepts.explanation: A sub-category within Scheduled Tribes characterized by a declining or stagnant population and the use of pre-agricultural level technology. The category was defined by the Dhebar Commission.

polity_articles.details: The President may specify the tribes or tribal communities as Scheduled Tribes (ST) in relation to any State or Union Territory.
Deals with the administration of tribal-majority areas under the 5th and 6th Schedules of the Constitution.

important_facts.fact: There are a total of 75 PVTGs in India, with the highest number located in the state of Odisha.
No Scheduled Tribe (ST) population is found in Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh, Delhi, and Puducherry.

sections.title: Largest Tribes of India
sections.description: The geographical distribution of India's major and largest tribes based on population.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Rajasthan, and Maharashtra
geographical_data.key_characteristics: It is the largest tribe in India. The word 'Bhil' is derived from the Dravidian word 'Billu', meaning bow.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Central India, primarily Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Maharashtra
geographical_data.key_characteristics: It is the second-largest tribal group in India. They speak the Gondi language, which belongs to the Dravidian family.
The third-largest tribe in India. Their language, Santhali, is officially recognized and included in the 8th Schedule of the Indian Constitution.

important_facts.fact: According to the 2011 Census, Madhya Pradesh has the largest tribal population in India in terms of absolute numbers.

sections.title: Tribes of North-East India
sections.description: Prominent tribes found in the North-Eastern states, known for their distinct cultural heritage.

key_associations.extra_info: The Bodo tribe is the largest indigenous ethno-linguistic group in the Brahmaputra Valley.
These tribes are well-known for traditionally following a matrilineal society structure.
Historically, there has been a geographical and cultural division between the hill-dwelling Kukis and the valley-dwelling Meiteis.
These tribes are named after the major hills and geographic features of the state where they reside.
This is the only tribe classified as a Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) in Tripura.

sections.title: Tribes of Andaman-Nicobar and South India
sections.description: Unique tribal groups residing in the island territories and the Nilgiri Hills.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: They are among the most isolated tribes globally and fall under the PVTG category. The Sentinelese still remain largely uncontacted by the outside world.
Famous for their pastoral buffalo rearing culture and the traditional practice of fraternal polyandry.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Nallamala Hills, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
geographical_data.key_characteristics: They are traditional hunter-gatherers who speak the Chenchu language, a member of the Dravidian language family.

sections.title: Major Tribal Festivals and Historical Rebellions
sections.description: Nature-centric festivals celebrated by tribes and their major uprisings against exploitation during the British era.

historical_events.significance: A massive uprising in the Rajmahal Hills led by brothers Sidhu and Kanhu against British authorities, zamindars, and moneylenders.
A rebellion in the Chhotanagpur region led by Birsa Munda against the exploitative zamindari system and British colonial policies.

key_associations.extra_info: A major nature festival celebrated by the Munda, Oraon, and Ho tribes, primarily involving the worship of the Sal tree.
Often called the 'Festival of Festivals', it showcases the rich culture, dances, and traditions of various Naga tribes.
A major spring festival and traditional marriage market celebrated enthusiastically by the Bhil tribe.
